imprimis5:

Look. We're playing a card game about people wearing tights and wielding patently impossible powers. Let this slide.

The powers are only patently impossible in the universe we live in; SOTM's setting has time travel, mystic dimensions whose different physical laws "leak" into our world, alien genetic meddling and more.  In that context, simply contradicting what we know of real-world physics isn't an issue in the slightest; the only things that are weird in such a context are things that don't make sense no matter how much phlebotinum is involved.  This isn't quite such an issue yet, but it's something that has to be explained.  Otherwise, It Just Bugs Me.

Frankly, I can accept "comic book science" MUCH more easily than I can accept some examples of Comic Book Fashion Sense.  The authors can be forgiven for not having a doctorate-level understanding of the jargon terms they pepper their technobabble with, but it's much harder to comprehend how anyone ever thought that looked cool, for various possible values of that.

Take the Freedom tower.

 

If you are fighting in Megalopolis and someone hides behind the Freedom tower so you can't shoot them, it's a minor inconvenience.  They are using the Freedom Tower to protect themselves from you.

It's a very diferent story if they run into the freedom tower.  Now the Freedom tower becomes a much bigger obstacle, and in fact a series of big obstacles that you have to deal with.

 

The same for MDP.  Baron is using his MDP's to distract the heroes and buy himself time.  Until those giant floating platforms are dealt with you can't get to Blade.

It doesn't take as much to get past an MDP as it does to get onboard and hunt someone down.

That's how you get a 10hp device vs. an entire environment deck.

 

The current deckbuilding game involves a mash-up deck of Vengeance Baron with all his platforms, and his -2 damage dealt to devices on the MDP.
